items.b: SHANGHAI DIAMOND EXCHANGE SIGNS BEIJING PACT WITH THREE GOVERNMENTS
items.t: Botswana, Namibia and South Africa signed the Beijing Declaration on 15 September. De Beers chief executive Al Cook witnessed it; eight Chinese retail brands attended without signing.

items.b: HONG KONG SETS Q1 2027 FOR CENTRAL GOLD CLEARING
items.t: The Policy Address also implements a half-rate tax on physical commodity trading and has the HKMA exploring a larger Exchange Fund gold holding.

items.b: SWISS WATCH EXPORTS RISE 9.1% IN AUGUST, US SHIPMENTS FALL 19.4%
items.t: August shipments reached CHF 1,789.2m on one extra working day. The United States fell to CHF 197.5m while the United Kingdom rose 46.1%.

items.b: US LUXURY STORE OPENINGS FALL 46% TO 123,334 SQUARE FEET
items.t: JLL counted the first half of 2026 against 227,000 square feet a year earlier. Jewellery and watch retailers took 43.5% of the smallest size band.

items.b: INDIA RAISES GOLD HALLMARKING FEE TO RS 75 AN ARTICLE
items.t: The gazette of 14 September sets a Rs 200 minimum per consignment and leaves silver at Rs 35. Indian outlets put the previous gold rate at Rs 45.

items.b: VICTORINS LISTS OVER 250 LOTS FOR ITS 20 SEPTEMBER SALE
items.t: A Cartier Libre Noeud diamond watch carries $52,500 to $105,750 and a Patek Philippe Calatrava $27,000 to $53,850, both the house's own estimates.

items.b: STAR DIAMOND NAMES JEAN RAYMOND BOULLE II CHIEF FROM 1 OCTOBER
items.t: He succeeds Lester Kemp, interim chief executive since November 2025, at the Fort à la Corne kimberlite project. No financing or resource figure accompanies it.

All four are lower against the 16 September marks in Carat Capital's own record.
